explanation: Represent work as (node, processed) stack entries. Push the right child, left child and a marked copy of the node, in that order. The LIFO stack then emits the root before visiting the left and right subtrees.
timeComplexity: O(n+1): each node creates a constant number of stack actions and is emitted once.
spaceComplexity: O(h+1) auxiliary pending-action stack for tree height h, plus O(n) returned values. Worst-case h=n.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/tree_preorder.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The stack records the remaining traversal actions in reverse execution order. Expanding a node schedules exactly root, left subtree, right subtree, because the most recently pushed action runs first. A marked entry emits its value once instead of expanding again; null entries do nothing. Each real node is expanded and emitted once, so exhausting the stack returns every value in the required order.
walkthrough: For the tree with root 8, left child 4 (whose right child is 6), and right child 10, emit 8, enter the left subtree and emit 4 then 6, then enter the right subtree and emit 10. Result: [8,4,6,10]. The explicit marked entry delays each emission until its scheduled turn.
edgeCases: An empty tree returns an empty list.
Repeated values are emitted once per node; do not deduplicate.
A skewed tree has height n, so pending-stack space can be linear.
